questions.q: What is the programme mainly about?
options: A new way of dealing with the dead called water burial
Why people are afraid of dying and how to feel calmer
Funeral traditions in different countries around the world
How to recycle old coffins and wood from cemeteries
questions.why: Neil says they'll be discussing water burial, compared with burial and cremation.

questions.q: What problems with traditional burial does Dan mention?
options: It is too expensive and slow for most families today
It releases dangerous mercury into the air and water
Coffins use up forests and cemeteries are getting full
Families don't like visiting graves in bad weather
questions.why: Dan says the US uses four million acres of forest a year for coffins and cemeteries are overcrowded.

questions.q: Why does Neil first think cremation is better?
options: It is cheaper
It doesn't need any space
It is faster than any other method
It uses no energy
questions.why: Neil says 'with cremation, there's no space needed', so it must be better.

questions.q: According to reporter Sahar Zand, what is wrong with cremation?
options: It takes several days
It leaves nothing for the family
It is not allowed by most religions
It releases toxins and uses a lot of energy
questions.why: She says toxins such as mercury can be released, and one cremation could heat a home for almost a week.

options: The body is buried at sea far away from the coast
The body is frozen in water and then broken into pieces
The body is burnt on a fire next to a river or lake
The body is heated in alkali liquid until only bones remain
questions.why: Dan says the body is put into an alkali solution heated to 150°C, leaving only the skeleton.

questions.q: What advantages does water burial have over cremation?
options: It needs no computer or trained staff to run it
It takes about four hours and uses much less energy
It is free for families who can't pay for a funeral
It keeps the whole body in the same state as before
questions.why: Dan says it takes only 4 hours and uses much less energy.

questions.q: What could happen to artificial implants after water burial?
options: They could be reused by people in poorer countries
They must be buried with the skeleton in the grave
They are destroyed completely in the process
They are sold to hospitals in the UK for research
questions.why: Sahar says they come out almost as good as new and could be sent to the developing world.

questions.q: What happens to the skeleton at the end?
options: It is given to science for students to study
It is buried in a small grave near the family home
It is ground into dust and given to the family
It is put into the sea in a special ceremony
questions.why: Dan says it is ground into dust and put in a jar for the family, like a cremation.
